subject: Lighting inside and around cabinetry
hook: Fitter, electrician, fitter, electrician: the order that hides cables.
ig:
Fitter, electrician, fitter, electrician: the order that hides kitchen lighting cables.

Most visible cables in a kitchen come from one thing: the lighting was decided after the units went in.

In a typical project the sequence looks like this:
1. Lights, switches and drivers marked on the kitchen drawings
2. Your electrician's first fix, running cables to those points
3. Cable routes made in the panels in our workshop
4. Units installed by our own team, cables fed through
5. Your electrician's second fix and testing

It only works if everyone works from the same drawings, which is why we share ours.

Swipe for each stage. Planning a kitchen this spring? Tap the link in bio and see how our bespoke kitchens are made.
fb:
Kitchen lighting with no cables on show comes down to one thing: doing the work in the right order.

This carousel shows a typical sequence: lighting marked on the drawings, the electrician runs cables, we make the cable routes in the workshop, we install, then the electrician connects and tests. Everyone working off the same drawings is what stops cables appearing where they shouldn't.

on_asset: F1: Design — Light positions, switches and driver spots marked on your kitchen drawings alongside the units. | F2: First fix — Before units arrive, your electrician runs cables to the agreed points, using our drawings. | F3: Workshop — Cable holes and routes made in the panels in our Hanley workshop, before the cabinets are assembled. | F4: Install — Our team fits the units and feeds the cables through the planned routes, with nothing cut into finished panels on site. | F5: Second fix — Your electrician fits the lights, connects the drivers and tests every run. | F6: Finished — Clean lines of light, no visible cables, drivers you can reach. Concept images throughout.
